handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, built, or decided in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

session_context.focus: Analyzed all T36–T47 test results job-by-job. Extracted prompts from m3_infer.py to separate files. Made 4 Gemini prompt fixes based on findings. Identified session 10.3's sidewalk_sides change as the primary regression driver. Also analyzed T50 (Expo) and T55 (Solara) from the new test wave.

this_session.summary: Two parts. First: extracted all three inline prompts from phase1/inference/m3_infer.py into phase1/inference/prompts/ (gemini_prompt_pdf.txt, gemini_prompt_image.txt, system_prompt.txt) and updated the script to load them from files. Second: analyzed T36–T47 test outputs end-to-end — read every Gemini extraction JSON, read case library actuals, and diagnosed root causes for each job. The dominant regression driver was identified as the session 10.3 sidewalk_sides change: Gemini now returns both_sides on 7/12 jobs, doubling sidewalk SF on large jobs and adding $50–$145K in error per job. Four fixes were applied to gemini_prompt_pdf.txt.

t36_t47_accuracy.note: Significant regression from T28–T35 wave (7/8 within ±10%). Primary driver was sidewalk_sides regression from session 10.3.

regression_identified.before_10.3: Sidewalk defaulted to road_LF × 5 (one side always). Conservative and mostly correct.
regression_identified.after_10.3: Sidewalk driven by Gemini sidewalk_sides field. Gemini returns both_sides on 7/12 jobs, including Forest Grove where the confidence note explicitly states the typical section does not show a sidewalk slab — inference was from ramp details instead.
regression_identified.dollar_impact: On a 3,642 LF road: both_sides = 36,420 SF vs one_side = 18,210 SF. At $4/SF = $72K difference per job. Multiplied across 7 jobs accounts for a large fraction of the observed regression.
regression_identified.fix_applied: Restricted sidewalk_sides source to typical section only. All other inference paths (ramp details, ramp counts, plan-view lines, scope notes) explicitly blocked. Ties go to one_side.

gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.issue: False positives on 5+ jobs (T37, T41, T44, T46, T47). Gemini was triggering on road profile grade changes, pad elevation callouts, demolition scope, and earthwork notes — none of which indicate lot grading.
gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.fix: Rewrote guidance with explicit false-trigger list. Requires a dedicated grading sheet showing contours into lot interiors, OR plan notes using exact lot-grading keywords. Added caution that a false positive adds $70,000–$150,000. Reinforced null as the default.

gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.issue: both_sides returned on 7/12 jobs based on ramp details and other weak inferences rather than the typical section.
gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.fix: Added SOURCE RULE: typical section is the only valid source. Explicitly blocked: ped ramp details, ramp quantities, plan-view sidewalk lines, scope notes. Added tie-breaking rule: when ambiguous between one_side and both_sides, return one_side.

gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.issue: T43 Solara returned export_needed when actual project required import/borrow fill. Profiles showed proposed grade above existing (= fill needed) but Gemini called it export.
gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.fix: Added DIRECTION RULE block before disambiguation notes: proposed grade above existing = import_needed; proposed grade below = export_needed. Added lot grading caveat: when lot_grading_in_scope=true, road profile cuts alone don't represent full balance — default to unknown unless complete cut/fill table present.

gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.issue: T39 Painted Rock: Gemini counted full length of Midway Ave and McGuire Rd (existing roads being improved) rather than improvement zone only, adding ~78 LF.
gemini_prompt_fixes_applied.fix: Added EXISTING ROAD IMPROVEMENTS paragraph at top of road_LF_hint guidance: for improvement work on existing roads, count only the improvement zone using BEGIN/END CONSTRUCTION markers. If improvement extent unclear, set road_LF_confidence to low for that segment.

held_pending_decision.issue: False positives on T36, T44 (fired incorrectly); false negative on T43 Solara (12" water main present but called false). Proposed fix: require explicit pipe diameter label ≥10" on utility plan — wide ROW, fire flow notes, and connection to existing large main do not qualify.

per_job_root_causes.T36_Settlement_MT: Good result (+4.9%). Lot count undercount (-6) and road_LF undercount (-4%) offset large_diameter_water false positive. No lot_grading false positive saved it.
per_job_root_causes.T37_Killdeer_Meadows: Lot_grading false positive (+$110K), lot_count 31 vs 18 (+$59K), utility coverage hallucination 100% vs actual 32%/53% (+$86K), both_sides sidewalk (+$55K). Previously analyzed in full.
per_job_root_causes.T38_Expo: Under-estimate. Blow-off assemblies missing, wrong paving class (residential KP on commercial job), sewer coverage 50% vs ~95%, water unit price wrong, FH count 1 vs 2, ped ramps 2 vs 6. Previously analyzed in full.
per_job_root_causes.T39_Painted_Rock: Moderate over (+14.5%). Lot count correct. Road_LF slightly high from full Midway/McGuire length measurement. No lot_grading false positive. Earthwork import adds cost. Multi-use path not modeled.
per_job_root_causes.T40_Lone_Fir: Good result (+7.7%). Simplest job in set — rural road, no utilities. Road_LF overcount (+9.4%) explains most of the $32K error.
per_job_root_causes.T41_Woodman: Moderate over (+18.9%). ROW=88ft inflates all area-based items (ROW_SF = 88,000 vs likely 50×928=46,400). Lot_grading false positive adds ~$50-80K. Ballast=null (missing separate ballast line item).
per_job_root_causes.T42_Mountainside: Significant under (-28.2%). ROW=33ft drives area-based costs very low. Actual $439K for 4 lots at $646/LF implies terrain-specific earthwork not captured by standard $/LF rates. Lot_grading=false is correct but the model still misses actual site complexity.
per_job_root_causes.T43_Solara: Large under (-33.3%). Three Gemini misses compounded: (1) earthwork=export_needed vs actual import/borrow — import fill is 2-3x more expensive; (2) large_diameter_water=false vs actual 12" water main; (3) large_diameter_sewer=false vs actual 15" sewer main. All three now addressable with fixed prompts.
per_job_root_causes.T44_Raghorn: Large over (+58.8%). Lot_grading false positive + large_diameter_water false positive (adds premium water main on top of standard 8" main). Lot count +4 extra. Storm basins possibly overcounted.
per_job_root_causes.T45_6th_Ave: Moderate under (-11.9%). Road_LF severely short (700 vs 947 LF, -26%) because Gemini measured only profile grade-change zone on 6th Ave rather than full improvement length. This should improve with road_LF fix. Job is in Spokane Valley WA — KP is North Idaho rates. The undercount and market mismatch partially offset.
per_job_root_causes.T46_Boyds: Moderate over (+26.8%). Lot count and road_LF both accurate. Lot_grading false positive is primary driver (+$70-100K). Strip_haul_off=true is partially justified (demo scope) but may be over-costed.
per_job_root_causes.T47_Forest_Grove_PH2: Worst result (+100.6%). Lot_grading false positive on 3,642 LF job. Both_sides sidewalk on 3,642 LF = 36,420 SF (now fixed). Job is in Spokane WA — market/rate mismatch. Actual case library shows HAMMER ROCK BUDGET (hard rock excavation) — not a KP concept. Manifest lot_count=78 likely reflects total plat across all phases, not Phase 2 scope — Gemini's 24-lot count may be correct for Phase 2.

new_test_wave_analysis.note: Tests T48+ use gemini-3.5-flash (not gemini-2.5-pro). Extraction quality varies — some fields improve, others regress vs prior wave.

root_causes: Blow-off assemblies (4 EA) completely missing from estimate — no rule in system_prompt triggers them
Ped ramps (6 EA) completely missing — no rule triggers from curb_type + sidewalk_sides
Water main unit price KP median ($55.25/LF) too low vs actual (~$100+/LF for this job type)
Strip haul-off: null defaulted to stockpile but actual line item is INCL HAUL OFF (~$9K delta)
T50_expo.detrimental: Partially — missing line items (blow-offs, ped ramps) are Stage 2 rule gaps fixable by adding derivation rules. Water main pricing gap requires KP calibration. Estimator can add these quickly once flagged.

root_causes: Lot grading excluded (lot_grading_in_scope=null per new tighter rule) — but Solara's case library CONFIRMS lot grading IS in scope (STRIP LOTS, LOT EXC TO EMBANK, PLACE TOPSOIL on lots). New null rule is correct for false-positive jobs but excludes a real scope item here.

Earthwork: road corridor is export (10,000 CY net, explicit table) but lot areas require import borrow fill — both conditions are true simultaneously. Estimate only prices the road export, missing the lot borrow/fill cost.

Dual utility mains: actual has 15" sewer + 8" sewer AND 12" water + 8" water running separate segments. Estimate prices the large-diameter mains but may not correctly price the full dual-main configuration.
Asphalt pathway paving (separate pay item along Meyer/Railway), 60" drop manhole, ped ramps, blow-offs, mailbox pads — all missing.
T55_solara.detrimental: No — gap is explainable and verifiable. Lot grading is a known scope item Brian can confirm in 30 seconds. Dual utility mains are flagged by large_diameter fields. Estimator verification closes most of the gap quickly. This is exactly the use case: system surfaces the base estimate + flags, Brian adds lot grading + confirms dual main scope.

per_job_detrimental_assessment_next_step.goal: Go through each job one at a time and classify each gap as (A) detrimental — system gave wrong or misleading output that would cause a bad bid, or (B) verifiable — gap is explained, flagged, and an estimator can close it quickly.
per_job_detrimental_assessment_next_step.framing: A large % error is not automatically detrimental. Solara at -39% is non-detrimental if the reasons are transparent and the estimator can adjust. A small % error CAN be detrimental if it comes from a hidden offset of large over and under items that mask each other.
per_job_detrimental_assessment_next_step.status: NOT STARTED — this is the immediate next task
